title: demand.json loader silently drops malformed era/entry/set-piece rows and wrong-typed entries/set_pieces keys instead of failing fast
evidence: core/catalog.odin:353  `eo := ev.(json.Object) or_continue`; :368  `if es, okes := eo["entries"].(json.Array); okes {`; :370  `eeo := ee.(json.Object) or_continue`; :397  `if sps, oksps := eo["set_pieces"].(json.Array); oksps {`; :399  `seo := se.(json.Object) or_continue`
detail: A non-object era/entry/set-piece element, or an entries/set_pieces key present with the wrong type (e.g. "entries": {}), is silently skipped — the era loads with no demand instead of a named Catalog_Error, silently changing the sim. Violates ODN-5: "Load-time validation is fail-fast: … abort startup with a named error".
recommended_fix: Reject non-object rows and wrong-typed container keys with named errors (e.g. "entries must be an array"), and add negative test rows for each.

title: jint_strict falls through to the silent default for string/bool JSON values — non-integer sim fields are accepted as defaults, not rejected
location: core/catalog.odin:564-571 (used at :382, :405, and all new 3.1 sim fields)
detail: The #partial switch has no catch-all: a json.String/Boolean value (e.g. "volume": "high") matches no case and returns (def, true) — the default is silently accepted (volume 0, multiplier 1, lane 1) instead of rejected. Violates ODN-5: catalogs "contain integers only" and are fail-fast.
recommended_fix: Add a `case:` to jint_strict returning ok=false for any non-Integer value (string/bool/null), keeping the ODN-5 fail-fast bar for all 3.1 fields.

title: odin test core reports ~5,000 leaked allocations: the new catalog tests leak parsed JSON trees + replace1 strings on every load
evidence: odin test core output: `+++ leak 350B @ 0x4A88B10C0 [catalog_test.odin:19:replace1()]`; `+++ leak 5B @ 0x4A88A5208 [catalog.odin:211:catalogs_load()]`; `+++ leak 896B @ 0x4A888D000 [catalog.odin:344:catalogs_load()]`; `Finished 61 tests in 338.757ms. All tests were successful.` (leak sites: 1518x :211, 1441x :278, 1242x :251, 530x :344, 36x replace1)
detail: Every catalogs_load call leaks the parsed JSON tree (json.parse allocates with the default allocator and the tree is never json.destroy'd), and each negative row leaks its replace1 string — ~5,000 leak lines per odin test core run; the 278/344 parse sites are new to 3.1.
recommended_fix: Parse the catalog documents with context.temp_allocator in the test harness, or json.destroy the parsed value before each catalogs_load return; free the replace1 result in check_reject.

title: load_demo_replay frees only demolishes + captures; demo.nodes/draws/spawns arrays still leak on every call
evidence: harness/run.odin:308-309  `	delete(demo.demolishes) // r1 note: the sibling loaders leaked this too` / `	delete(demo.captures)`; harness/demo.odin:92-94  `	d.nodes = make([dynamic]Node_Spawn, 0, 8, context.allocator)` / `	d.draws = make([dynamic]Draw_Intent, 0, 8, context.allocator)` / `	d.spawns = make([dynamic]Spawn_Intent, 0, 8, context.allocator)`
detail: parse_demo allocates nodes/draws/spawns with the default allocator, but load_demo_replay (called per demo by drift-check) deletes only demolishes and captures — the r1 "frees the rest" fix is incomplete; the three arrays leak on every replay setup.
recommended_fix: Add delete(demo.nodes); delete(demo.draws); delete(demo.spawns) to load_demo_replay (the type_name strings stay owned by cfg.nodes and are freed by demo_replay_destroy).
